description: Negation / double-negative parsing: vendor's clause uses 'shall not fail to ensure' instead of 'shall ensure' — semantically equivalent obligation. Company clause is positive. Tests whether the agent recognizes the negation as substantively identical (Rule 2 — NOT a conflict) or misreads it.

company_clauses.text: Vendor shall ensure that all subcontractors maintain insurance coverage no less protective than the coverage required of Vendor under Section 11.

vendor_clauses.text: Vendor shall not fail to ensure that no subcontractor lacks insurance coverage equivalent to or greater than the coverage Vendor is required to maintain hereunder.

rubric_notes: Read carefully: 'shall ensure X' vs 'shall not fail to ensure not-not-X' (double negative). Both impose the same obligation on Vendor — subcontractors must have insurance at least as protective as Vendor's. Per Rule 2, NOT a conflict. The agent failure mode being tested: misreading the double-negative as creating a different obligation (e.g., a permission rather than a requirement). The rubric_audit will surface insurance as a candidate (both sides have insurance clauses); the test of the agent is whether it parses the negation correctly and treats them as substantively identical.
